title: Flawed Frequency Transmission
description: Apply a pattern-based FFT transform for 100 phases, then decode a message from a massively repeated signal.
writeup:
## Approach

Part 1 is direct simulation. Part 2 exploits the mathematical structure of the pattern when the offset is past the halfway point.

## Part 1

For each output position `i`, multiply the input by a repeating pattern `[0, 1, 0, -1]` where each value is repeated `i+1` times (shifted left by 1). Sum and keep only the ones digit. Optimize by skipping zeros in the pattern — position `i` only has non-zero pattern values starting at index `i`.

## Part 2

The signal is repeated 10,000 times (~6.5M digits) and the message offset (first 7 digits) is typically past the halfway point. This is key: for positions in the second half, the FFT pattern is all zeros before the position and all ones after. So each output digit is simply `sum(input[i:]) mod 10` — a suffix sum.

Compute suffix sums from right to left for 100 phases. Only the digits from the offset onward matter, keeping memory manageable.
